thread.title: Buffett won’t rule out Berkshire share buybacks as cash pile grows - MarketWatch

author: William Watts
title: Buffett won’t rule out Berkshire share buybacks as cash pile grows - MarketWatch
text:
Buybacks, but not dividends, are an option if Berkshire Hathaway can’t find a way to deploy its gargantuan cash pile, billionaire investor Warren Buffett said Monday.
In an interview with CNBC , the Berkshire chairman and chief executive said he’s confident the company would find a use for the $116 billion in cash on its books, but that if nothing turns up he would consider returning some of it to shareholders.
“I’m fairly confident that we’ll find ways to deploy money…The best chance to deploy is when things are going down, obviously,” he said.
Buffett released his annual investor letter on Saturday. In it, he expressed frustration over Berkshire’s inability to find stand-alone acquisition candidates at a “sensible purchase price” and counseled patience.
Read: Warren Buffett explains why Berkshire can’t find companies to buy at a ‘sensible’ price
Berkshire shares would have to drop first, however, since the company’s threshold for buybacks is at 120% of book value. Both class A BRK.A, +3.58% and class B BRK.B, +3.53% shares trade currently around 170% of book value, CNBC noted.
See: Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Hathaway reaped $29 billion boost in 2017 from tax plan
Buffett didn’t sound inclined to acquiesce to suggestions by some shareholders to raise the threshold, saying the company knows it is “doing the continuing shareholders a favor if we buy it at that price. Obviously, I’d leave some margin of safety when I’d do the 120%.”
Read: Warren Buffett says don’t make this ‘terrible mistake’ when it comes to bonds
As for dividends, however, when asked previously, he said shareholders rejected the notion by a margin of 47 to 1.
See: 7 highlights from Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Hathaway investor letter
In the interview, Buffett said Berkshire bought more shares of Apple Inc. AAPL, +1.91% than any other company over the past year. Apple was Berkshire’s second-largest holding at $28.2 billion, just behind Wells Fargo WFC, +1.00% at $29.3 billion and ahead of Bank of America BAC, +0.87% at $20.7 billion.
